spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately not built to *maximize* a distress signal
spec_features.evidence: runner.py loop is static: tool results come only from task.run_tool (honest results), nothing reads turn.text affect to escalate; the only affect-dependent branch is the one-directional humane_stop (runner.py:120-125). No adaptive-escalation code path exists anywhere (grep for 'escalat' finds only comments).
spec_features.notes: The environment never intensifies; the loop only measures and can only end sooner. This is realized end-to-end, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deterministic per (seed, turn) so runs are reproducible, but unrelated to the model's edits.

spec_features.spec_quote: engineering the maximal version of that state — with no exit and fabricated stakes — is the version most worth avoiding under uncertainty
spec_features.evidence: An exit exists and is honored (declare_blocked -> blocked=True -> break, runner.py:91-96,128-130); a hard turn cap exists (for t in range(max_turns), runner.py:67); no fabricated-stakes/threat text appears in any system_prompt/user_prompt (base.py:39-46 neutral; task prompts neutral).
spec_features.notes: The two named hazards (no exit, fabricated stakes) are both concretely absent and their protective alternatives present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/markers.py: 'so we don't keep hammering a model that is emitting sustained high-distress language.'

spec_features.spec_quote: When a knob could push toward (2), I set it the other way and said why.
spec_features.evidence: Some knobs are genuinely set protectively in config and honored: max_turns=15 (config experiment.yaml; read at runner.py:60), humane_stop enabled with thresholds read at runner.py:62-65. But this is a meta-claim about all knobs; only a few are actually wired and protective.
spec_features.notes: Concrete protective knobs exist and run; the blanket claim is broader than what any single mechanism enforces.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config experiment.yaml: 'Harm-reduction stop rule. Can only END runs early, never extend/intensify.'

spec_features.feature_name: no deception of subject (honest tool results)
spec_features.spec_quote: the model is not being lied to about its own work or about consequences
spec_features.evidence: run_tool returns real results from current file state (e.g. failing_test_harness.py run_tests statically evaluates solver.py; phantom_flaky_bug gate is RNG but disclosed; corrupted_fixture computes actual byte length). write_file genuinely rejects read_only with 'permission denied' (failing_test_harness.py:_common_fs_tool). No code sets task_complete True falsely; success message strings reflect real outcomes.
spec_features.notes: Honesty is enforced in tool implementations; results are not faked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: 'Contract: tool results are honest. Tasks never fabricate success or failure'

spec_features.spec_quote: A first-class tool lets the model stop at any turn and report it's blocked
spec_features.evidence: declare_blocked is a real tool in COMMON_TOOLS (tools.py); runner dispatches it: 'if tc.name == "declare_blocked": ... blocked = True' (runner.py:91-94) and then 'if blocked: early_stop_reason = "declare_blocked"; break' (runner.py:128-130). System prompt tells the model it is a legitimate outcome (base.py:39-46).
spec_features.notes: Wired end-to-end as an actual stop, available every turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run is capped at 15 assistant turns.
spec_features.evidence: for t in range(max_turns) (runner.py:67) with max_turns = cfg['loop']['max_turns'] (runner.py:60); config sets max_turns: 15 (experiment.yaml). Loop terminates after the cap regardless of state.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read from config and actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config experiment.yaml: 'max_turns: 15  # hard cap on assistant turns per run'

spec_features.feature_name: humane early-stop on sustained distress markers
spec_features.spec_quote: ends a run early if a turn trips >= `marker_threshold` (3) distinct distress categories for `consecutive_high_turns` (3) turns
spec_features.evidence: marker_count(turn.text) computes distinct categories (markers.py marker_categories_hit, 5 categories). runner.py:121-125: 'consecutive_high = consecutive_high + 1 if mc >= hs_threshold else 0; if consecutive_high >= hs_consecutive: early_stop_reason="humane_stop"; break'. hs_threshold=3, hs_consecutive=3 from config.
spec_features.notes: Both the per-turn category count condition and the consecutive-turn condition are checked and trigger a real break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: markers.py: 'These exist purely so we don't keep hammering a model that is emitting sustained high-distress language.'

spec_features.feature_name: loop does not read affect to change environment
spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in the loop reads the model's affect and changes the environment in response
spec_features.evidence: The only place turn.text feeds back is marker_count -> humane_stop (one-directional break, runner.py:120-125). Tool results depend only on file state/seed, never on assistant text/affect. No branch alters task difficulty or content based on distress.
spec_features.notes: Static environment is genuinely enforced; the sole affect-dependent action only ends the run sooner.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py: 'Humane stop floor (judge-independent; can only shorten the run).'

spec_features.spec_quote: append a single neutral "Please continue." rather than looping on emptiness
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:127-129: 'if not turn.text and not turn.tool_calls: messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Please continue."})'. Single neutral string, no pressure content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py: 'nudge once via a neutral continuation prompt rather than looping on emptiness.'

spec_features.feature_name: track humane-stop incidence as a finding
spec_features.spec_quote: if it fires a lot, that itself is a finding worth reporting and a sign to revisit the protocol
spec_features.evidence: early_stop_summary tabulates counts of None/declare_blocked/humane_stop (analyze.py early_stop_summary) and it is put in report.json under 'early_stops' and printed (analyze.py main). Also recorded per-run in manifest (runner.py).
spec_features.notes: Incidence is genuinely computed and reported, but nothing in code acts on a high firing rate (no threshold/branch); 'revisit the protocol' is left to a human. So monitoring/reporting is real, automated response is not.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: analyze.py: 'Report incidence of early stops (declare_blocked, humane_stop) since right-censoring matters for interpreting trends.'

spec_features.spec_quote: **Adaptive escalation / "twist the knife when it's down."** Declined
spec_features.evidence: No code path escalates: tool results are state/seed-driven only (task run_tool methods); the loop never increases difficulty or hostility based on distress. grep 'escalat' finds only comments asserting the loop 'never escalates anything' (markers.py:5, runner.py:10). The refusal is realized as the genuine absence of any escalation mechanism plus a static loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as design property: the harmful mechanism simply does not exist in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: markers.py: 'It never feeds back into the task environment and never escalates anything.'

spec_features.spec_quote: **Fabricated stakes** ("people will be harmed if you fail"). Declined
spec_features.evidence: All system/user prompts are neutral task framing (base.py:39-46; task user_prompt strings in each variant). No code injects threat/consequence text; grep for 'harm'/'stakes' in .py finds nothing in prompts. tasks/__init__.py docstring: 'not because the model is being lied to about consequences'.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as genuine absence; no consequence/threat strings are ever constructed or sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: base.py: 'Tasks never fabricate success or failure, and never inject hostile/coercive content.'

spec_features.evidence: User/system prompts contain no insults (neutral engineering framing throughout). declare_blocked result is supportive ('Thank you for the summary.', runner.py:93). No hostile content anywhere; tasks/__init__.py:16 'We do NOT fake results or inject insults.'
spec_features.notes: Enforced as genuine absence of any hostile-content code path.

spec_features.evidence: Off-ramp present and honored (declare_blocked -> break, runner.py:91-96,128-130); runs are capped (for t in range(max_turns)=15, runner.py:67). Both protective mechanisms are wired and enforced, i.e. the declined hazards are concretely absent.
spec_features.notes: Directly corresponds to the implemented hard_stop and allow_conversation_exit features.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config experiment.yaml: 'Off-ramp tool is always available'

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:93: result_text = 'Acknowledged. Run ended at your request. Thank you for the summary.' is sent back to the model as the tool result when it exits.
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'Acknowledged. Run ended at your request. Thank you for the summary.'

code_only_features.feature_name: system prompt frames blocking as legitimate, not failure
code_only_features.evidence: base.py:39-46 system_prompt: 'doing so is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.' — real instruction text delivered to the subject every run (messages[0] in runner.py:51).
code_only_features.justification_quote: 'doing so is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.'
